passage: “Me first! Me first!” Nkechi shot up from the reading mat, arm stretched so high her shoulder shook. The teacher held up a paper star. “The star goes round the circle. When it reaches you, it's your turn.” Nkechi sat, hands squeezed between her knees, bouncing. Hana had the star first and passed it on. Nkechi watched each pair of hands it went through, lips pressed together. When it finally reached her, she took a big breath and began, “My dog...”

qa.q: What object went round the circle?
qa.a: A paper star went round the circle.

qa.q: What was Nkechi feeling while she waited for the star?
qa.a: Eager and excited to share, with some impatience: she bounced and pressed her lips together with her hands squeezed between her knees. She may also have worried her idea would be forgotten.

qa.q: How did the star rule help Nkechi?
qa.a: It gave a clear, fair signal for when her turn would come, so she had something concrete to watch while she waited.

qa.q: How might Hana see Nkechi's jumping up?
qa.a: Hana had the star first and may have felt watched or a little rushed by an eager friend, or she may simply have been excited too. Nothing in the scene says which.

grounding: Eagerness shows as jumping up and shouting me first; a turn-taking rule helps manage the wait.

passage:
“Who can tell me the colour of the sky?” asked Zainab Miss.
Rehana's hand shot up before the question ended. “Me, me, me first!” She hopped from foot to foot, then half stood, fingers wiggling.
“Rehana, I see your hand. Let's take two hands first, one at a time.”
Rehana sat down, but her arm stayed up, held at the wrist by her other hand. Two children answered. Then Zainab Miss said, “Rehana.”
“Blue... and grey when rain comes!” she burst out.

qa.q: What question did Zainab Miss ask?
qa.a: She asked, “Who can tell me the colour of the sky?”

qa.q: What does Rehana holding up her arm with her other hand suggest?
qa.a: She is eager to answer and trying to hold herself in during the wait. It could also hint at some nerves about being chosen.

qa.q: What small step helps eager children like Rehana wait?
qa.a: Saying that you see the raised hand and how many turns come first, as Zainab Miss did, so the wait has an end.

qa.q: What might the two children who answered first feel?
qa.a: Perhaps pleased to be chosen, or a bit rushed with Rehana hopping beside them. 🙂

grounding: Eager preschooler shouts me first; a clear turn rule helps.
